bibl.title: Auditory temporal masking: an electrophysiological study of single neurons in the cat's cochlear nucleus and inferior colliculus

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: The mechanism of forward masking may be due to the postexcitatory inhibition of some slow-adapting neurons and to synaptic inhibition for fast-adapting ones.

span.label: auditory temporal masking
span.quote: The physiological mechanism of auditory temporal masking was studied by single-unit analysis in the cat's cochlear nucleus and inferior colliculus.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: The recording system for neuronal activity was conventional; single-unit activity was recorded extracellularly by a tungsten microelectrode and stored on magnetic tape for subsequent off-line computation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A faint probe tone drives an abnormally long response latency in collicular neurons, so the probe's discharge arrives at or after the discharge evoked by the following noise burst and is absorbed into it, which produces backward masking
span.quote: In the backward masking situation with a masking interval of 0 msec, the latency in response to noise bursts calculated from the beginning of the probe tone becomes 20msec. Accordingly, the unit does not elicit backward masking in the case of a latency of less than 20msec in response to the probe tone.

span.label: Only a small number of collicular units showed backward masking, so the effect rests on few cells.
span.quote: The number of units that showed backward masking in the inferior colliculus was relatively small.

span.label: Recordings were made under anesthesia and restraint; the authors say further work in unanesthetized, unrestrained animals is needed for the higher auditory centres.
span.quote: Further study under unanesthetized and unrestrained conditions will make it possible to explore the mechanism of masking at these particular regions.

span.label: A possible fourth mechanism (feedback inhibition from higher levels) could not be demonstrated with the present methods.
span.quote: In addition tothese modes, inhibition due to a feedback loop from upper levels may take part in backward masking as a fourth mode,

span.label: simultaneous masking
span.quote: Simultaneous masking refers to the situation in which masked and masking stimuli are presented concurrently.

span.label: temporal masking
span.quote: On the other hand, it is assumed that temporal masking may be related to the neural mechanisms in the higher auditory system.

span.label: backward masking
span.quote: Backward masking may involve central processes because it was not demonstrable in the cochlear nucleus.

span.label: cochlear nucleus
span.quote: Backward masking may involve central processes because it was not demonstrable in the cochlear nucleus.

span.label: **THE DISTINCTION IS PSYCHOLOGICAL AND THE ARGUMENT IS ANATOMICAL.** `From the psychological point of view TWO KINDS of auditory masking are known, that is, SIMULTANEOUS and TEMPORAL masking` - a split made by psychophysics, which this paper then tests by asking where in the cat's auditory pathway each one appears. **A behavioural taxonomy checked against anatomy**, which is the move Carlesimo2004 makes for priming thirty-three years later and mcmahon-olson2007 makes for repetition suppression
span.quote: From the psychological point of view two kinds of auditory masking are known, that is, simultaneous and temporal masking.

span.label: **AND THE LOCATION IS ESTABLISHED BY AN ABSENCE:** `Backward masking may involve CENTRAL processes because IT WAS NOT DEMONSTRABLE IN THE COCHLEAR NUCLEUS.` Nothing was found at the first relay, therefore the mechanism is above it. **A null result at one recording site doing positive work** - which only holds because the same preparation DID show forward masking there, so the absence is not a failure of the method
span.quote: Backward masking may involve central processes because it was not demonstrable in the cochlear nucleus.

span.label: **IT IS THE PHYSIOLOGY OF marcel1983's INSTRUMENT, AND NEITHER CITES THE OTHER.** marcel1983 uses backward masking to render a prime unreportable and shows that semantic access survives it; this paper, twelve years earlier and in cats, asks WHERE backward masking happens and answers `not in the cochlear nucleus`. **One paper uses the tool, the other locates it.** The corpus holds both, and the pairing is only visible because they sit side by side - the sixth such pair found tonight
span.quote: On the other hand, it is assumed that temporal masking may be related to the neural mechanisms in the higher auditory system.

span.label: builds-on → ELLIOT (1962a)
span.quote: For monotic conditions of forward and backward masking, the parameters of the stimulating sounds used were the same as those employed by ELLIOT (1962a).

span.label: extends → ELLIOTT (1962a, b) and PICKETT (1959)
span.quote: As shown in Fig. 8, the relationship between the amount of masking and the masking interval between the probe tone and the noise burst shows tendencies similar to those in the psychological data of ELLIOTT (1962a, b) and PICKETT (1959), although the curves indicate some differences from neuron to neuron.

span.label: backward masking —distinct-from→ cochlear nucleus
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **AN EDGE BUILT ON AN ABSENCE, AND THE AXIS IS DOING THE WORK.** The sentence asserts that backward masking WAS NOT DEMONSTRABLE in the cochlear nucleus - a negative finding, and `no-change` is the only value in the enforced axis vocabulary that can carry it. Weight 0.9 because `may involve central processes` is the authors' inference from that absence and their hedge is in the quote. **A reader taking the triple alone gets `these two are distinct`, which is true but loses that the distinctness IS the finding** - the note has to say so, and this is the third time tonight that `distinct-from` has been the nearest available type rather than the right one.
span.quote: Backward masking may involve central processes because it was not demonstrable in the cochlear nucleus.

span.label: histogram
span.quote: stimulus time (PST) histograms were made from the spike data for quantitative measurements.

span.label: Forward masking weakened as the interval between the noise burst and the probe tone grew at both recording sites, but the decline was more abrupt in the inferior colliculus than in the cochlear nucleus.
span.quote: The amount of masking (lower figure) decreased with longer masking intervals as in the cochlear nucleus, although in general the decrease was more abrupt in the inferior colliculus (see also Fig. 8).

span.label: Backward masking in the inferior colliculus took three forms: "on" neurons with a long latency to the probe tone (6 units), neurons inhibited by the noise burst (3 units), and "off" neurons (2 units).
span.quote: (1)" on" type neurons with long latency to the probe tone (6 units); (2) inhibition by noise bursts (3 units); and (3)" off" type neurons (2 units).

span.label: A unit produced backward masking only when its latency to the probe tone exceeded the 20 msec at which the noise burst's own response arrived, so units responding within 20 msec showed none.
span.quote: In the backward masking situation with a masking interval of 0 msec, the latency in response to noise bursts calculated from the beginning of the probe tone becomes 20msec. Accordingly, the unit does not elicit backward masking in the case of a latency of less than 20msec in response to the probe tone.

span.label: The single-neuron curves relating amount of masking to masking interval followed the same trends as the published psychophysical masking data of Elliott and Pickett, although individual neurons differed from one another.
span.quote: As shown in Fig. 8, the relationship between the amount of masking and the masking interval between the probe tone and the noise burst shows tendencies similar to those in the psychological data of ELLIOTT (1962a, b) and PICKETT (1959), although the curves indicate some differences from neuron to neuron.

span.label: Only a small proportion of inferior collicular units showed backward masking at all.
span.quote: The number of units that showed backward masking in the inferior colliculus was relatively small.

span.label: Fast-adapting neurons form the overwhelming majority of neurons in the inferior colliculus.
span.quote: supposition is strongly supported by the recognition that fast-adapting types of neurons have an overwhelming majority in the inferior colliculus

span.label: "off" type neuron
span.quote: In "off" type neurons neuronal responses occur after th e cessation of the tone bursts,

span.label: masking interval between probe tone and noise burst
span.term: masking interval between probe tone and noise burst
span.quote: As seen by comparison of the upper sample records at the center and right, the response to the probe tone appeared again as the masking interval was increased.

span.label: amount of masking (threshold shift in dB)
span.term: amount of masking (threshold shift in dB)
span.quote: The amount of masking (lower figure) decreased with longer masking intervals as in the cochlear nucleus, although in general the decrease was more abrupt in the inferior colliculus (see also Fig. 8).

span.label: stimulus intensity in dB
span.quote: Because backward masking was found in the neurons showing "on" response with long latency to the probe tone, the stimulus intensity vs. the latency of neuronal responses was examined along the auditory pathway from the cochlea up to the medial geniculate body (Fig. 9).

span.label: latency of the neuronal response
span.quote: The latency shifts at3,500Hz at four different intensity levels are shown byarrows: 14.5msec at-30dB,

span.label: 36 — number of inferior collicular neurons tested for backward masking, of which 11 showed it in three modes
span.quote: Backward masking was examined on 36 inferior collicular neurons. Among them, 11 units manifested effects of backward masking in three major modes:

span.label: 6 units; 3 units; 2 units — how the 11 backward-masking units divided across the long-latency "on", noise-inhibited, and "off" modes
span.quote: (1)" on" type neurons with long latency to the probe tone (6 units); (2) inhibition by noise bursts (3 units); and (3)" off" type neurons (2 units).

span.label: more than 20msec / 10msec — the unit's response latency to the probe tone inside the backward-masking region versus its latency to the noise burst
span.quote: Under the stimulus condition within the shaded areas, the latency of this particular unit was more than 20msec, and the latency to the noise burst (-10dB) was 10msec in this unit.

span.label: 14.5msec at-30dB — measured response latency at 3,500 Hz at the highest of four tested intensities, the shortest of the reported latency shifts
span.quote: The latency shifts at3,500Hz at four different intensity levels are shown byarrows: 14.5msec at-30dB,
